turnaround_reason: Inspire fell ~58% from ~$147 to ~$61 as GLP-1 drugs (Zepbound approved for OSA) created a competitive overhang and CMS coding/reimbursement disruptions cut into revenue (Q2 2026 rev -7.6% to $200.6M). Profitability and cash flow still beat, the company launched 'Project Horizon' and raised its 2026 outlook, and the Inspire V rollout is underway.
bullish_points: Still profitable with cash flow beating expectations despite the revenue dip; raised 2026 outlook
Reimbursement/coding disruption is viewed as progressively de-risking through 2026 — a fixable, not structural, headwind
Inspire V launch and ambulatory surgery center penetration are concrete growth levers; management argues GLP-1s expand the diagnosed OSA funnel long-term
Clean balance sheet ($321M cash vs only $29M debt); modest net insider buying (net +32k shares)
bearish_points: GLP-1 adoption is a real near-term revenue headwind the company itself acknowledges, and some physicians now try GLP-1s before Inspire therapy
Forward P/E ~40 vs trailing ~13.5 implies the market expects earnings to fall — rich on forward numbers
Revenue is still declining and the stock sits ~9% below its 200d MA — basing, not recovering
Single-product concentration in a category facing a structural pharma alternative
catalyst: CMS reimbursement/coding normalization plus Inspire V ramp re-accelerating revenue growth in 2H26
catalyst_timing: Progressive through 2026; next quarterly print is the key checkpoint on reimbursement recovery
suggested_trade: Small starter spot; wait for one clean quarter of reimbursement normalization before sizing up. Liquid options (ATM IV ~71%) allow defined-risk expressions.
key_risk: GLP-1s structurally shrink the addressable implant market faster than Inspire V and funnel expansion can offset
would_skip_if: Next quarter shows reimbursement headwinds persisting and revenue declines steepening
